utterances.text: No. Hadzici was quiet at the time. There was no shooting, no shelling, and the only thing was that the schools were open until mid-April. Then they would open for a day or two and then they would close, and then finally the classes stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it not true that the only students left in the classroom were the Muslim students in Sarajevo, because all the Serbian students had left, had they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. There were quite a few Serbian children there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you stated also that there was no organised defence of Bradina, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. As I said, there were just village sentries. I can illustrate what the defence was like by giving you a fact, that Bradina was in the middle of the Muslim territory, and according to the 1991 census Bradina had 602 inhabitants from the newborn babies until people the age of 90, and I don't see how it could have resisted the onslaught around it of the mass of people, 50-60,000 Muslims and Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did state there was no organised defence, did you not? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also stated that none of the Serbs in the village were armed, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I stated that I did not have any weapons myself, but there were people who had some hunting rifles. Some even had military rifles or pistols, for which they had permits from the former State.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the people that had those M-48s, they had permits too, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I just said -- maybe the interpretation is not good -- there were people who had army rifles. I don't know where they got them from. I spent only a short while in Bradina, from 8th May until 27th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that's the key there. You did not arrive in Bradina until May 8th, and the arming of Bradina had occurred much before that, had it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay, but you did tell this Tribunal that the people guarded their houses, so they had to have some kind of arms, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again you repeat the same thing. I said that some people had hunting rifles and some had army rifles. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: It is not the way to put your questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know where they got them. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: It is not the right way.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: I will rephrase the question, your Honour. You also said that the Muslim forces attacked Bradina, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said that these were the forces both composed of Muslims and Croats. I assumed that on the basis of the insignia they had on their -- some had camouflage uniforms; some had black uniforms. Some had the checker board on theirs and some had the Crescent and the star on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the chequerboard is clearly HVO; is that right? That is the Croatian military symbol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact another group of military soldiers, the MUP, also participated in this attack on Bradina, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I don't know who belonged to what type. I don't know anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated, I believe, that when you were taken to Celebici you were beaten with all kinds of tools. It included -- you used the term the apple of a rifle, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I do not know if you ever saw the rifle. It has the part where you close the chamber when you enter the bullet into the chamber and you can take it off, and then at the side where you can hold it in your hand it is rounded. This part is called the apple, and that is the part that I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you were never in the military service, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so your experience with a gun, did it just occur in Bradina in May?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. In my college, teaching college, we had a course in all people's defence. It was very -- a long time ago in 1963, 64, when I was in the third or fourth year of my course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Going back to that apple, that apple is the little round lever when you put in the rifle shell into the chamber and you close it back, that is the little round thing about this big; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, since you were from Bradina and you knew that some of the Serbs in your town were armed, you knew a Zarko Mrkajic, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zarko Mrkajic? Yes, I did know him. He had a cafe in Bradina, if that's the man you referred to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were aware that he was responsible for distributing the arms to the Serbs in Bradina from the SDS, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also did not know that Rajko Djordjic was also responsible for distributing arms in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, because I lived in Upper Bradina, as we called it, and it's about 2 or 3 kms away from the centre. There was no gasoline at the time, so I didn't even go down to the centre at all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling this court you were not aware of the promise by the Serbian forces to come and liberate Bradina, are you? Are you telling them you did not know about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. How would I know that. There was no electricity in Bradina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you also stated that you were -- this was from Thursday's testimony -- that you were severely beaten in Bradina, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, in fact, they made you -- they beat you first, let you get on the truck and then they took you back off the truck again for another beating, did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those were the HVO/TO forces, MUP forces that arrested you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. These were the forces wearing camouflage military uniforms. I don't know to which formations or units they belonged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, it was then at Bradina upon your arrest that all of your valuables were taken off you; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not have much with me. I just had a watch. I don't know if you would consider that a valuable. Cigarettes and a lighter and that is all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said then you were taken to Celebici. I believe -- is this still May 27th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was the third day of the attack on Bradina, because it began on May 25th, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You claimed that when you were taken into Celebici, you were taken off the truck and you were lined up against a wall there near the gate; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then you also claimed that you were beaten by a group of Muslims. Is that not what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your face is totally against the wall and you were not allowed to look back at these people, so you did not know who they were, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, they told you to say: "Praise the Lord!", did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. We had to repeat that the Muslim faith was the best. We had to use the greetings "Selam Aleikam Merhaba!" We had to repeat -- well, I don't understand those words. I don't know if they understood them themselves -- entire soura from the Koran and it was a horrible humiliation. The entire Celebici echoed with our voices. We had to shout at the top of our voices.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Gligorevic, I want to just kind of come to an agreement with you. I understand you have a lot of information to give to the tribunal and I believe on Thursday and earlier today you were able to tell them whatever you wanted, but now I want to ask you to please listen to my question. If you listen to my question and just answer my question, then we will both be out of here real soon; okay? Is that a deal?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. If I know the answer, I will give up the answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: they also had you say: "Praise the Lord!", did they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It happened several times right at the beginning, and then it stopped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And "praise the Lord!" is more of a Croatian, Catholic saying, is it not? It is not Muslim?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated that you were beaten -- some of the people in the line there were beaten with a stone from the Neretva river. Is that not what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the Neretva river does not go by Celebici, does it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's not very far from the camp, several hundred metres from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But that is Lake Jablanica, is it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when there is lots of water in there, but when there is not -- I mean that stone there is not only in the middle of the river. You can find it also elsewhere around on the river side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also told the court you know a man named Gojko Miljanic, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Or should I say did you not? I am sorry. He was from Bradina, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew him as a man about 60 years old; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Thereabouts. I think he must have been born in 1934. I think so, yes, 1934.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. On May 27th this Gojko Miljanic was beaten in Bradina. He was beaten on the way to Celebici and he was beaten there at the gate of Celebici. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know how much beatings he got in Bradina, because he was further away from me in the column, and he entered -- he boarded the car before me, but I know everybody was beaten. The elderly people got beaten less, the younger people much more, but at Celebici yes, I saw the man in the line-up where we stood, and he gave no sign of life all the time. In that state he was when he carried him to the Hangar Number 6, and only the day after he died late in the afternoon without ever regaining consciousness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he died on May 27th/28th as a result of his beating on May 27th; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. He died on 28th May as consequences of his beatings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was no other Miljanic at Celebici that was killed during your stay there, was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You also told us that at night guards would come to the door and call people out, and you said that they were afraid to come in at night, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. These night visitors, but our guards, the guards who usually guarded us, would not go inside hangar 6. Those who came at night were not guards. I don't know where they came from. I remember what I told last Thursday, there was a group. They introduced themselves saying: "We are from Sarajevo." Were they really from Sarajevo? I don't know. I suppose they were. They took away Stravko Gligorevic and a person named Milosc, whose family name I don't know. They beat him up in front of us and then they took him away. Later on we heard that Milosc, as he was an elderly person of poor health, he was killed at Igman and Stravko was killed in the prison at Stravanica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The fact these guards or strangers would come at night to the door and call someone else, the truth is what happened outside the hangar you yourself do not know. You do not know who did the beating and you do not know if there was beating. You only know someone came out in one condition and they came back in another. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know who was beaten. I do not know who beat them outside.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People were taken out at night and ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were also taken in for interrogation at the first of your stay in Celebici, where you were asked certain questions. Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The kind of -- I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. I was more or less in the last, group one, but the last who went for interrogation and last time I described what it looked like behind the command building, where we were there on the pavement, and we were interrogated there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask you the kind of questions they asked were questions like: "Did you have arms?" And "are you a members of the SDS?" Is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They asked those kinds of questions and gave the answer straightaway. They ask you the question straightaway and then they answer it straightaway. They write it down in that way, and they had to sign it afterwards, because whatever I said it wasn't correct. They said: "No, no, I know that is how it is." I had to sign up and even sign in Cyrillic script, which was severely forbidden in Konjic at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I am not familiar, so I am not going to ask you about those, but when you say you have had an opportunity to review that statement since then, have you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't know where I could do it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean, you have never seen the statement that you signed at Celebici in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you: you also stated on Thursday that you eyewitnessed a lot of incidents involving mistreatment at Celebici, did you not? In fact, one of the people was Miroslav Vujcic. He was killed trying to escape the first day at Celebici, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was killed from firearms. He was shot when we were lined up against the wall. He was among those who were, apart from being beaten regularly he was taken out of that line-up and ordered, as with some others, to lie down, and they were hit and beaten with rifle butts and shovel handles. I don't know. Probably he could not bear those beatings. He jumped up and the only thing we heard were the cries of the guards: "He's running away! he's running away!." Then we heard some shots. We were saying to ourselves: "Well, this person ran away." I suppose they assumed some other people would try the same thing and when we were going towards Hangar Number 6 after all those beatings, I saw him lying down on the grass.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was May 27th, 1992, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, May 27th.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were taken to Hangar Number 6 shortly thereafter, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would just like to go into a little description of Hangar Number 6 now, if you do not mind. How large would you say it was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can't tell you exactly. I think some 15-20 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The only windows in Hangar Number 6 were about 3 metres high, were they not? You could not see out of them, could you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. These were small, very narrow windows towards the upper part of the wall, just behind -- beneath the roof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You sat on the back left-hand wall. The front wall was a series of large doors that were never opened, were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were two large doors there, but they started to open them only in the autumn after the Red Cross intervened because of great heat. The middle door was also big and there was a smaller part that opened -- the only part that opened was a smaller part in that big door.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Those big doors that are along the front of Hangar Number 6, they did not have any holes or anything in them with which you could look out, did they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Around the bottom you sat on the edge of the hangar. There was no space between the wall and the floor where you could reach your hand out, was there? It was sealed from the wall down to the concrete, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was no major type of opening. Only water could go through.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. As far as toilet facilities, there were toilets that had been dug towards the back of the hangar on the right-hand side that you all would use during the day; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes we would use them; sometimes not. It depended on the guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At night there was a large bucket put inside the hangar for your actual use that was taken out during the day, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Not at the beginning, but later on there were two such containers that would be taken out in the morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see you are shaking your head before I am finished with the questions. Do you understand some English?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A little.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: A lot more than my Serbo-Croatian, I am sure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that there was a very little water at Celebici for you all to drink, but you stated before that sometimes you were allowed to splash your face with water; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That was at the beginning. Later on when the heat was at the greatest, it was very difficult to get any water. In my case, and those people who were sitting around me, our situation was the most difficult because we were sitting at the top and the door was far away. Konjic is very hot in the summer. We perspired a lot. We needed quite a lot of liquid and we did not have that. We were very many, many of us, 240 or thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were provided with salt during that period too to keep you from losing so many liquids, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe you have stated on Thursday that when the prisoners were brought back in and they had been beaten, you would rub salt on their bruises; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Some of them. That is out of the detainees some people had parents living nearby, and some of them knew the guards. They used to work with them previously. So they would pass on some food. Later on even visits were admitted, first of all once a week, then twice a week and then again just once a week. Those people who had some family, that family was able to bring some kind of food or blankets or some clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I want to go back to a specific date, and I know you are not real clear on specific dates, but this may bring to mind the date that all this occurred. You said that all of the prisoners were beaten after July 12th; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: July 12th has a significance to it, does it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It is a Serbian religious holiday, Saint Peter's day, Petko Dan, if that is what you mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was not what I meant, but I have just been educated. Thank you. That was also the day I believe that the military police were murdered somewhere around Bradina; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know who killed whom, but according to what the guards told us there was a van up there with I don't know how many policemen in it and also some inhabitants from Repovci were there. It was hit by a shell. Then what I heard at Celebici and later on at Musala, the Serbs were apparently accused of it, as if these were the remains of some Serb resistance around there, but later on it turned out that it wasn't correct. There was some kind of internal rows and the guards later on admitted it. It is just that because of that we were beaten for several weeks very severely at Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because of the significance of that July 12th, when that happened, that is the fact on July 12th the guards were told that Serbians had done that, even though it may have turned out later that they had not committed this crime, on July 12th that is what they believed, was it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. How should I know that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you were not told why you were beaten on July 12th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Precisely because of that they were accusing some people from Bradina. For example, Miso Kuljanin and some others that were at the municipality in Hadzici, currently at that time held by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you knew that Mr Landzo had gone to the scene of the murder of these military police, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Who would tell us? Who? We were not even allowed to raise our eyes while they were there, let alone ask a question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now Bosko Samoukovic was beaten on July 12th, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dusko Samoukovic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Bosko Samoukovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bosko Samoukovic, not on that day. It happened later, towards the end of July. I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could I have the usher put the prosecution exhibit on the ELMO, the one that the defendant drew, please -- I mean the witness drew? I do not know if mine is as clear as their original. That would be fine with me if you have the original one of these. Now just for clarification's sake, you are sitting at the middle of the wall to the left in hangar 6; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now, I believe you had stated that Mr Cecez was sitting against the wall; is that not what you stated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I simply said where he was when he found him dead in the morning. That was here. I think he used to sit somewhere there opposite the door. I can't tell you exactly. There were quite a few of us there, and he did not spend a long time in Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, Mr Cecez was sitting -- I am going to show you -- in this line; he was sitting somewhere in here?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe in one of the middle lines, yes, middle rows, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the man called Keljo, he was also sitting in the middle line, too, was he not? He was not sitting against the wall, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At first he was sitting against the, there in the corner, more or less here, while he was -- how shall I say -- while he was convalescing, while his ribs were broken, and when he got slightly better, then he changed his place. He was maybe from time to time even privileged in being able to go out and have a cigarette with some of the guards, not with all of them. According to what he said, they asked money from him because they thought he had money, as before the war he had his own cafe in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, this Keljo, as you said, he was invited out by the guards to have cigarettes, and I am going to jump ahead in my questioning. The night that he was killed by the bullet, you know that a guard came in crying and that was an accidental shooting, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. I was up there far away. Maybe that is why I do not know some of the stories. The hangar is very, very big, some 40 or 50 metres. We were not allowed to walk around, so I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I would like to ask you: you also said before that you saw the guards and then seemed to be afraid of coming in to where the prisoners were at night; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. That was the case at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, there were only two guards on duty at one time guarding 240 prisoners; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: How many guards were there I don't know or where they were placed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to go back to Bosko Samoukovic. I am sorry if I massacre these names. I will try harder. On the drawing there on the ELMO will you please show where he was standing when he was beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Here in front of the entrance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. You stated that you were not allowed to go into the JNA because you have poor eyesight; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not go and serve in the Yugoslav Army because of that reason.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated on May 27th when you were arrested you were forced to take off your glasses and stomp on them in the road; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All you had was a twisted frame from then on; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The frame remained on the road.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were sitting at the very back of the hangar; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You never had any glasses during the time you were at Celebici, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but I would just like to say that my eyesight is not so bad for me not to be able to recognise a person I have known for 40 years even if the distance is a bit... More important, he was a friend of mine, Bosko, and he was married to a cousin of mine. I knew him very, very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you are near-sighted, are you not? You cannot see at a distance. So am I.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I can recognise a person I have known for years.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated that you witnessed the torture of Momir Kuljanin. Is that not what you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if Momir Kuljanin said in his statement that this occurred outside the hangar, is he lying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know what he stated, but I just know that the palms of his hands were burnt and he had large blisters on both hands. I can only say that I saw inside the hangar the burns. I saw when it was done to Dusko Bendjo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So as far as Momir Kuljanin is concerned, you did not see what actually happened to him; you saw the results; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because whatever happened to him happened outside the hangar, outside of your presence, did it not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also stated that you did witness some torture of a Dusko Bendjo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you know he is not coming here to testify, is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I object to that question. It is not proper to discuss who is coming and who is not coming to testify. We do not know that for sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have been allowed to discuss it with every witness. They say "so and so can tell you better because he is coming to testify" so evidently they know. If he knows, then he is able to answer. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: The question you asked was suggesting the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Yes, in cross-examination. I hope it does. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: It was completely telling him the answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: May I ask it again? JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Well, if you want to.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Mr Gligorevic, you know that Dusko Bendjo is not coming here to testify, is he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. In fact, I don't know where he is now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You do know that he escaped from Musala and that he ended up killing a guard, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Musala? No, that is not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, as far as you discussed the other day, a Simo Jovanovic, did you not, and you said he was called out by Zenga, but the truth is that you do not know what happened outside the hangar, do you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All I know is what I heard with my own ears and that is his moanings and screamings and what happened afterwards, after he was carried back into Hangar Number 6, and who did it outside I can't tell.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. As far as -- you said you were good friends with Cedo Avramovic, who was also a teacher; is that not true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Not that we were very good friends, but we were acquaintances.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He lived in Celebici, did he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As an acquaintance, you know that he had two sons that were members of the BH army, or the TO in Sarajevo, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Well, I worked in Hadzici in those years and he worked in Celebici, and we wouldn't see each other for a couple of years maybe. I don't even know how many children he had. I know that his daughter was a teacher. I don't know about his sons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't know that he have gave two automobiles to the TO, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you didn't know that the people who brought Mr Avramovic to Celebici were HVO soldiers, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know that really.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you did state on Thursday, I believe, that no guards had come into the hangar the night that Cedo Avramovic died?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, we were all asleep. I didn't hear anyone come in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now you did not see Esad Landzo at Celebici before the middle of June, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before mid what? I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not see Esad Landzo at the Celebici camp as a guard before the middle of June 1992, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was there before that. I don't know that for sure, but he was there before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you do not know for sure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that Mr Landzo left Celebici camp towards the end of July, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. In early August. I know that because two of my relatives were the last people that he beat, and it was on the 2nd or 3rd August.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you saw Esad Landzo while you were at Musala, did you not, in January of 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Musala?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You did not know that he was a guard at Musala from June 1993 until April of 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTBERG
utterances.text: I did not understand what time we were talking about.

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: June -- I am sorry. January 1993 through April of 1993. I am sorry. He was a guard at Musala, was he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked about the beatings that went on after like July 12th. The guards were ordered to do those beatings, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know. How would I know?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They were following orders as a rule, were they not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again I have to repeat I don't know. The same answer as to your first question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I pass the witness, your Honour. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Any other questions? Mrs Residovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Can I ask him one more question, your Honour, just one more? The last time you saw Mr Landzo at Celebici was around 2nd or 3rd August; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Yes. Ms Residovic, you can now cross-examine. Cross-examination by Ms Residovic. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): May it please the court, Mr Gligorevic, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My name is Edina Residovic. I am the defence counsel for Mr Zejnil Delalic. Mr Gligorevic, I will ask a few questions and in order to clarify some events to the Trial Chamber and to the defence, some of the events that you testified about before this court. I will try to make my questions short and clear, but if I do not manage to do that, please indicate as soon as possible so that I can rephrase my questions in such a way that you are able to understand me. In relation to my questions and your answers, I will also make a very short note that my learned colleagues did not have to make. We both speak the same language. We understand each other and we could ask the questions and you could give the answers very quickly. However, both my question and your answer need to be interpreted, so that the court can understand and follow, as all the other participants in the proceedings. Since I am sometimes warned by the Trial Chamber about that, I would like to ask you if you could wait for a while after I ask the question so that the question can be interpreted in full and I will also try to wait for a while for your answer to be interpreted. I think we agree on that. Mr Gligorevic, when you testified before this court, you unfortunately stated a fact that was very hard for you, and that is the fact that you are one of those people who remained in prison for the longest period of time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In fact, you can confirm that you were arrested on 27th May?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1992, and that only in October 1994 you were exchanged with 87 -- actually 85 other Serbs from Musala?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. When you testified I noticed that you mentioned the word "arrest." We sometimes use the word "capture" or "taken prisoner", but I think it is all the same which word we want to use. The Trial Chamber will make the decision on what your status was on the basis of the entire proceedings and the evidence presented therein. Can you confirm before this court that during your stay in Celebici and later on in Musala that several hundreds of Serbs were detained there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yet, as far as I remember, you also testified that many of those were not detained for such a long time as you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell this court when the first prisoners were released, the prisoners who had been brought in Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that they were transferred to Musala. There was a group of elderly people and I think they were transferred maybe even before mid-June.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that immediately after the arrest a substantial number of people who had been arrested were released?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. As far as I know a few people were released. Maybe two or three persons that I know. Maybe also some people that I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does it mean, Mr Gligorevic, that there were some criteria according to which some people were released and the others detained?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. It was simply a question of knowing somebody, either from work, and the groups of people that were transferred to Musala, I suppose that the only criterion was their age.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also testified that you were not a participant in the resistance in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is also true that you were not organising the defence of any kind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us or can you confirm is it true that some people had a personal reason for detaining you for such a long time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I used to work in Bradina for a very long time. Since 1975 I worked at Repovci. Maybe you know the village better. It was a Muslim village. I worked in Kravici. It was a Croatian village. I worked for six years there. Nobody ever said a harsh word about me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you maybe have a conflict with the official authorities in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I said I worked my land in Bradina. Since 1975 I lived in Hadzici municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the commission that questioned you for a very short time categorised the prisoners in some way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard about it, but nobody told me anything about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that somebody made a mistake when putting you into the category that determined your status?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Gligorevic, in 1996 you gave a statement to the prosecutor and on Thursday you testified that you were questioned only on one occasion and that was in Celebici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You stated then that there were three people who questioned you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was only one person, a person wearing a camouflage uniform. He was dark-haired, very rare hair. That's the only thing I know of him. I never saw him afterwards. I don't know his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is not true if somebody was to state there was a larger number of people who questioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, there was only one person who questioned me, but there were other people who interrogated other people elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified before this court that as far as you were able to gauge it, this questioning was just a formality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. It was done behind the building crouching on the pavement, and if the judge is at the same time asking questions and writing down answers without me saying anything -- JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: You are still falling into the same temptation of your dialogue with him. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honour. It's obvious that sometimes we forget ourselves and I will try not to do that in the future. We will have to slow down with our questions and answers. You stated that during this formal questioning that was just a formality you were not abused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, apart from the threats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was all happening outside of the building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time and at no other time you were told the reason for your arrest; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Nobody told me anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were never charged with anything. You also testified that you were just asked questions about weapons and some formations in Bradina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you still do not know the reason why you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You testified before this court that on 8th May you arrived from Hadzici; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would the questions about the weapons that you were asked and the fact that you arrived from Hadzici could be the reason for your detention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think so. I don't believe it, because while we were taken to Celebici, nobody was looking at who was actually guilty of something or not. The only thing that was important was to round up all the Serbs, young and old. So they were all brought to Celebici.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr Gligorevic, you said that you wrote the statement in Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not the statement. The statement was written by the person who questioned me. I simply signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You state that you usually signed in the Roman alphabet?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That moment I would have certainly used the Roman alphabet. JUDGE KARIBI WHYTE: Ms Residovic, we will have to stop here. You will continue cross-examination tomorrow morning. MS RESIDOVIC (in interpretation): Thank you, your Honour. 17 18

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 5.30 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 2nd day of April, 1997 at 10.30 a.m. 23 24 25
